title: UndoRedo history mismatch error when working with Resources that contain NodePath
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible: v4.4.1.stable.official [49a5bc7b6] ### System information Godot v4.4.1.stable - macOS Sequoia (15.6.0) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M1 Pro (Apple7) - Apple M1 Pro (8 threads) ### Issue description Hello I'm fairly new with Godot and I'm currently trying to leverage the editor and some script to configure characters in my game. In particular is the use of Resources in a `CharacterBody2D`, and how they store `NodePath`s. Specifically I noticed that if I'm trying to `@exports` for a specific `Resource` that contains an `@export_node_path` field, when I try to include the `CharacterBody2D` in another scene, the following error keeps popping up: ``` ERROR: UndoRedo history mismatch: expected 1, got 3. ERROR: UndoRedo history mismatch: expected 1, got 3. ``` Honestly I'm not sure why this happens, I didn't see any documentation that states that I can't use NodePath inside a resource, which leaves me scratching my head. It doesn't seem like a big issue, but it does clutter the Output and make it confusing to debug other problems. I left a video that shows how to reproduce the issue: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee9dcd38-f5dd-48cc-9c67-c9091adc721a ### Steps to reproduce ## Create a Resource Script 1. Create a resource script that has the following: ```gdscript class_name ResourceTest extends Resource @export_node_path("Sprite2D") var test_path: NodePath ``` ## Creating Character Scene w/ Resource 1. Create a `CharacterBody2D` scene. 2. Add a `CollisionShape2D` to the scene. 3. Add a `Sprite2D` to the scene. 4. Add a `Node` to the scene . 5. Add a nested `Node` to the one added in previous step. 6. In the new nested `Node` attach a new script that looks like the following: ```gdscript extends Node @export var resource_test: ResourceTest ``` 7. In the Inspector window add a `NewResouceTest`. 8. In the `NewResourceTest` select the `Sprite2D` as the path value for `Test Path`. The Scene Tree should look something like: ## Adding the new CharacterBody2D to a separate Scene. 1. Create a new 2D Scene. 2. Add the `CharacterBody2D` that was previously created. 3. Add another Node to the scene 4. Move the `Character4Body2D` node in the scene tree. 5. You will see the following error in the output: ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) Project that can reproduce the issue: - [nodepath-resource-bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22002078/nodepath-resource-bug.zip)
